I am in Quzhou County in southern Hebei, and at the start of the season I will follow the pattern that fits my place, my age, and the work I can manage steadily. I will keep the main wheat-maize rotation, because that is the safest and most familiar way for me to use the land, spread labor across the year, and keep grain coming from both seasons. I will not make the plan too complicated. I want crops that I know well, that match the local climate and irrigation conditions, and that do not require too much fine management. So I will keep winter wheat already on the land through spring and early summer, then after harvest I will plant summer maize on the same fields. I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize because I want stable yield and good stand establishment. I will use moderate fertilizer, not excessive fertilizer, because I want to control cost and avoid wasting money. I will irrigate wheat more often than maize, because wheat here usually needs more water at key stages, while maize can often do with fewer irrigations if the rain is normal. I will use rotary tillage after harvest because it is easier and lighter for me than deep ploughing every season, and it fits quick turnaround from wheat to maize. I will spray only as needed, mainly to keep weeds, aphids, and common diseases under control, because I want to protect yield without doing unnecessary work.
